items.summary: An authentication bypass in Canonical's LXD and MicroCloud lets a remote attacker impersonate any trusted client without holding that client's private key, by attaching the client's public certificate to their own TLS chain. Fixed in LXD 6.10.1, 5.21.9, 5.0.11 and 4.0.15 and MicroCloud 3.4.1 and 2.1.5; no known exploitation as of October 30.

An integer overflow in the Onigmo regular-expression engine used by GitLab's CI/CD configuration processing lets an unauthenticated attacker execute arbitrary code on a self-managed GitLab server. CISA added it to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on October 29 after probing of Alpine Linux's instance; patch to GitLab 19.2.8, 19.3.5 or 19.4.2 and confirm the underlying Ruby is fixed.

A use-after-free race in the Linux kernel's IPv4 TCP connection handling can be triggered remotely without authentication, and Anthropic demonstrated unauthenticated root command execution against a multipath TCP listener in a lab setting. Fixed kernels include 5.10.272, 5.15.223, 6.1.190, 6.6.159, 6.12.113, 6.18.56 and 7.2.10; apply the distribution kernel update and reboot.

An unrestricted upload of files with dangerous types in Adobe Commerce and Magento Open Source can allow remote code execution. CISA added it to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on October 27; apply the vendor patch as a priority.

An out-of-bounds write in Google's Brotli decoder (versions 1.0.3 through 1.2.0) is being exploited in the wild and was added to CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on October 27. Update every product embedding Brotli, including browsers, servers and libraries, to a fixed decoder build.
